title: Latvia's Historic Election Victory Masks a Fragile Compact Between Security… · 10 Oct
keywords: Latvia, election, United List, Andris Kulbergs, security politics, fiscal consolidation, inflation, NATO, European Union, Ukraine, Baltic states, cost of living, public spending, defence, economic policy
notes: Latvia's governing United List secured its strongest post-independence election result, winning 35.3 percent of the vote and 42 of 100 parliamentary seats, cementing Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs's pro-European, pro-NATO course. Yet the result tells only part of the story. With consumer prices still 3.2 percent higher than a year earlier and fiscal consolidation looming, the government's durability will depend on whether security credibility can translate into tangible improvements for households.
